transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-07-16 15:00 UTC
Duration: 43 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Moran (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Ben Hart (Vellichor HoML), Sana Kapoor (Vellichor Platform Eng), Liam O'Rourke (Vellichor CTO)

Summary: discovery call focused on reserved GPU capacity, tenant isolation, warm-pool / burst handling, and compliance constraints. Customer wants predictable latency for realtime scoring plus nightly batch jobs.

Topics: reserved capacity sizing, isolation topology (segregated nodes vs soft multitenancy), warm-pool strategy, prewarm costs, KMS/encryption, SOC2 + export controls, POC timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya on the call — SE focused on performance. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Ben: Hi Alex, good thanks. Excited to dig in, we have a bit of urgency — prepping infra for Q4 launch.
[00:17] Liam: Morning, everyone. Quick note — we're evaluating hosted vs dedicated vs private but leaning dedicated if isolation is good and burst works.
[00:30] Priya: Great. Can we start with a quick rundown of your workload shape? Batch vs realtime, model sizes, qps expectations?
[00:40] Sana: Sure. High-level: two main workloads — realtime chat scoring (1–2k qps at peak across clusters), and nightly offline vectorization jobs that spin up heavy load for several hours. Models are mix of 20B and 70B variants, we quantize to int4 for production.
[01:05] Ben: The realtime path is latency-sensitive — p95 under 150ms including some small prompt templates. Nightly jobs can be opportunistic but we want predictable throughput.
[01:16] Alex: Good context. For dedicated, are you looking for reserved G P U counts, or reserved pools with prewarm/warm nodes? And do you need single-tenant hardware or is tenant-level isolation OK?
[01:30] Liam: Single-tenant hardware would be ideal for compliance, but cost is a constraint. We'd accept node-level isolation with strict tenant fencing if we can get audit logs and KMS integration.
[01:42] Priya: Understood. Our Dedicated offering supports both — fully isolated nodes (physical tenancy) and logically isolated pools (tenant fencing). The tradeoff is cost and prewarm overhead.
[01:50] Sana: Can you expand on prewarm? We don't want cold-start spikes in the morning.
[01:56] Priya: Absolutely. We have a warm-pool concept — a set of GPUs kept hot with model kernels and KV caches loaded. You can reserve warm capacity and then burst onto extra ephemeral nodes when traffic spikes. Warm pools reduce cold-start latency but increase steady-state cost.
[02:15] Ben: What's typical prewarm sizing? Like how many GPUs per 1000 qps?
[02:21] Priya: Ballpark: for our optimized runtime with batching, 1 to 2 A100-equivalent GPUs serve ~500–800 qps for a 20B quantized model with p95 under 150ms, depending on prompt length. For 70B it's closer to 200–350 qps per GPU. Those are fuzzy — we'll need your exact prompt length distribution.
[02:43] Liam: That helps. Our p50 is low but p95 spikes when long context comes in. Also we have a SUITE of reranking requests that are prior to final output, those are short and high qps.
[02:58] Alex: Makes sense. A few questions on security: do you have data residency requirements and what KMS/HSM controls do you need?
[03:06] Liam: UK and EU residency for certain customers, SOC2 is must, and we'd prefer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-key) for model inputs. Also audit logs for inference requests at least 90 days.
[03:20] Priya: Redwood Dedicated can run in your VPC or private deployment for residency. We offer KMS integrations with AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and customer HSM options in Private installs. Audit logs and per-request tracing are available through the Console.
[03:34] Sana: Will that include token-level cost breakdowns? Our finance team insists on per-route chargebacks.
[03:39] Alex: Yes — we provide token-level metering and per-route dashboards. That ties into quota enforcement too.
[03:44] Ben: Back to burst — how does Redwood handle overcommit? Suppose ephemeral nodes are unavailable, do you fail open to hosted models?
[03:55] Priya: By policy you can define fallbacks: either queue requests (up to X seconds), degrade to a smaller model variant, or route to hosted Redwood instances. We usually recommend a mix — canary to smaller quantized variant then hosted only as last resort.
[04:12] Liam: For SLA reasons we don't want silent fallback to hosted instances due to data residency. We need explicit routing rules that prevent egress.
[04:21] Priya: Understood — that's straightforward: set a policy that disallows hosted fallbacks for those customers. We'll log rejected requests and surface alarms.
[04:31] Ben: Cost — curious about warm-pool pricing and burst unit costs. Also what's the billing model for reserved GPUs? Unit-hour reserved vs committed monthly?
[04:39] Alex: Reserved is committed monthly with discounts for 12/24 month terms, and warm-pool is an add-on for reserved capacity — you pay for warm hours but bursting ephemeral capacity is billed on-use. I'll send the pricing sheet.
[04:50] Sana: Could you show an example estimate for our anticipated 2k qps peak?
[04:55] Priya: Quick estimate: if you target 2k qps composed of 1.2k for 20B and 800 for 70B, you'd need roughly 3–4 GPUs for 20B and 3 GPUs for 70B in steady warm pool, plus a burst buffer of 4–6 ephemeral GPUs for headroom. So reserved pool ~7–8 GPUs warm, burst capacity incremental. Again, will refine with exact profiling.
[05:22] Ben: That's useful. What about autoscaling granularity — per-GPU or per-instance? How fast does scale up happen?
[05:29] Priya: We do continuous batching and fine-grained scheduling; scale-up to ephemeral nodes is subject to provisioning latency — with prewarmed images and warm pools we can get new nodes ready in ~30–90s. Cold provisioning from scratch is longer (3–5min).
[05:44] Liam: We need ~99.9% of production requests below p95 150ms — will warm pool + batching meet that SLA?
[05:52] Priya: With correct sizing and warm pools, yes — our internal benchmarks show p95 under 150ms for similar workloads. We'll run a bench with your traffic to validate.
[06:01] Sana: On the compliance side, are there any export-control concerns if we run models that are fine-tuned with customer data?
[06:08] Alex: Good callout. For Private deployments we can isolate entirely; for Dedicated we have data-in-transit and at-rest encryption and options to disable model caching outside the tenant. We'll need to confirm specific export-control regimes with legal.
[06:22] Ben: One thing — our ops team wants to avoid large blast radius when someone accidentally schedules a giant offline job. Can Redwood enforce tenant-level quotas and job-level throttling?
[06:32] Priya: Yes. We support per-tenant quotas, route-level limits, and scheduling windows. Offline batch jobs can be restrained to epsilon bandwidth to prevent impacting realtime. We also provide alarms and automatic shedding policies.
[06:45] Liam: What's your approach to network isolation on Dedicated? We run in our VPC but want git-like flow for deployments, and some teams need direct SSH/console for debugging.
[06:55] Priya: Dedicated in-VPC includes a customer-managed subnet, and we support bastion/jump hosts for admin workflows, RBAC for access, and SAML SSO. For Private on-prem we provide a more direct admin plane if that's required.
[07:09] Ben: Any reference customers with similar scale and compliance needs?
[07:13] Alex: We can share anonymized case studies — a couple of health-tech and fintech customers run mixed 20–70B workloads on Dedicated with warm pools and KMS BYOK; I'll include those references.
[07:24] Sana: On telemetry — priya, will we be able to ingest custom traces into our Datadog?
[07:29] Priya: Yes, we expose traces via OTLP and can forward to Datadog or Splunk. Also per-request metadata is exportable.
[07:36] Ben: Are there any setup timelines for Reserved? How long from signed contract to first reserved nodes live in our VPC?
[07:43] Alex: Typically 2–6 weeks depending on procurement, networking, and region capacity. Private on-prem is longer due to install windows.
[07:51] Liam: Procurement question — do you support term commitments that include burst budgets baked in? For example, commit to 10 GPUs but have a burst buffer of 20h/month at a fixed rate.
[08:02] Alex: Yes, we can structure burst addendums to include prepaid burst credits or capped burst hourly rates. We'll propose a couple of contract flavors in the pricing doc.
[08:14] Sana: For the POC, we want to test warm-pool effectiveness. Priya, can you outline a minimal POC plan?
[08:21] Priya: Minimal POC: 1) Redwood provisions a dedicated test pool in your VPC (3 GPUs) with models loaded; 2) Customer runs a representative traffic replay for 2–4 hours including peak spike tests; 3) We collect p50/p95/p99, cold-start times, and cost per token. Estimated checkout time ~2 weeks from kickoff.
[08:42] Ben: That fits. We also want to test failure scenarios — flaky nodes, heavy batch jobs during peak.
[08:48] Priya: We'll include chaos scenarios in the test plan and show fallback behaviors.
[08:53] Liam: One more — does Redwood support hardware affinity for particular GPU types (A10G vs A100)? We tuned kernels on specific silicon.
[08:59] Priya: Yes, you can request hardware classes. We try to honor affinity for Dedicated pools; availability depends on region and capacity.
[09:08] Alex: Ok let's capture next steps — I'll collate pricing, sample contract variants, and references. Priya will produce the POC runbook and benchmark template. Ben/Liam will share traffic profiles and compliance list. Any other items?
[09:22] Sana: We need a short diagram showing the isolation topology options — single-tenant vs tenant-fenced.
[09:28] Alex: Noted, I'll attach a topology diagram.
[09:32] Ben: One more small ask — do you support encrypted request-level payloads where only HSM can decrypt? That's critical for one customer.
[09:40] Priya: With Private deployments yes; for Dedicated we can integrate with your HSM for key unwrap and hold payloads in encrypted form. We'll validate specifics with our security team.
[09:53] Liam: Great. I'm comfortable moving to a POC if the contract includes BYOK and the no-hosted-fallback policy for selected tenants.
[09:59] Alex: Sounds good. We'll circulate the documents this week and aim to kick off the POC the week of 7/27.
[10:07] Ben: Thanks all. Quick note — our legal will want a list of SOC2 artifacts and penetration test cadence.
[10:13] Alex: I'll include SOC2 report location and pen-test cadence in the security pack.
[10:17] Sana: Thanks — talk soon.
[10:20] Meeting end.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription mis-labeled a few proper nouns (Vellichor sometimes transcribed as "Vellica"), occasional dropped words, speaker overlaps at ~02:40 and 08:40.

References mentioned: pricing sheet (link to be sent), POC runbook (Priya to share), topology diagram (Alex to attach), warm-pool benchmark template (Priya to share).
